title: Zeryab Estates
lede: Zeryab Estates is a private luxury retreat nestled in the heart of Marrakech, Morocco — a city where centuries of Andalusian, Berber, and Arab cultures converge into something singular. The brief called for an identity that could hold all of that weight without collapsing under it.

blocks.label: 01 — The Place
blocks.title: A Sanctuary Beyond Time
paras: The property is defined by its relationship with time: ancient craft traditions, living architecture, and a natural landscape that has resisted change. The brand needed to speak to a discerning international audience while remaining deeply rooted in its place of origin — not as nostalgia, but as lived continuity.

Heritage and nature frame every experience at Zeryab. Palm-shaded courtyards, Moorish arches reflected in still water, the scent of aged cedar and orange blossom — the identity had to translate this sensory world into a mark that travels across every material surface with the same quiet authority.

images.alt: Zeryab Estates logo over a Moroccan heritage painting

blocks.caption: Marrakech · Moorish Heritage — Zeryab Estates

blocks.label: 02 — The Inspiration
blocks.title: Centuries of Craft
paras: The logomark draws from two of Morocco's most enduring visual traditions: the pointed Moorish arch and the interlocking geometry of Zellige tilework. Both carry the same underlying logic — infinite complexity generated from a single, precise rule. The arch frames space; the Zellige fills it. Together they define the visual language of Moroccan sacred and domestic architecture.

The mark abstracts these references into a singular geometric emblem: an arch outline that, on closer inspection, reveals a Zellige-derived interlocking pattern at its core. It reads immediately as place without resorting to ornamental cliché. It is architectural, not decorative — structured, not nostalgic.

Typography was equally deliberate. Extensive exploration of letterform weights, spacing, and proportion resulted in a custom-spaced wordmark that balances the geometric rigidity of the mark with an open, breathing quality. The letters feel carved rather than printed — solid enough for embossing, refined enough for fine stationery.

blocks.caption: Logomark Inspiration — Zellige Geometry & Moroccan Arch Form
Typography Explorations — Custom Wordmark Development

blocks.label: 03 — The Identity
blocks.title: Heritage Reimagined
paras: The final identity system is built around the architectural logomark — a clean geometric form that holds its own at any scale, from embossed collateral to signage, from a wax seal to a digital favicon. The wordmark ZERYAB ESTATES uses wide-tracked uppercase lettering with custom spacing that gives the name the presence of an inscription.

Six brand colors extracted directly from the Marrakech landscape — deep navy, dark umber, olive gold, sand tan, deep terracotta, and burnt red — form a palette that feels simultaneously timeless and specific to place. These are not decorative choices; they are materials translated into color: the charcoal of hammered iron, the warmth of hand-pressed clay, the oxidised gold of aging copper.

The system was designed for permanence. Every decision was tested against the materials it would live on: heavily textured papers, metallic foils, raw clay surfaces, woven textiles. The identity performs equally at the two extremes of luxury hospitality — the intimacy of a guest welcome card, and the authority of an architectural façade plaque.

blocks.label: 04 — Colors & Typography
blocks.title: The Palette of Marrakech
paras: Each color in the system was chosen for its resonance with the physical world of Marrakech — the deep navy of tile shadow, the umber of cedarwood grain, the gold of polished brass lanterns, the tan of sun-dried clay, the terracotta of handmade bricks, the burnt red of poured iron. The palette reads cohesively across print and digital, in natural light and candlelight.

Typography bridges the historical and the contemporary. Display text uses elegantly spaced uppercase lettering with fine optical adjustments — a voice that belongs in both a riad guestbook and a contemporary art catalogue. Body text remains restrained and readable, giving the display work room to breathe.

blocks.label: 05 — Visual Applications
blocks.title: Where the Brand Lives
paras: A luxury hospitality brand earns its credibility through the quality of its physical touchpoints. For Zeryab Estates, every printed piece was approached as a craft object — not a reproduction of the identity, but a new expression of it. The weight of the paper, the depth of the emboss, the warmth of a hand-applied wax seal.

The application system spans stationery, welcome collateral, hospitality amenities, textile branding, and architectural signage. Each surface demanded a different interpretation of the core mark — sometimes reduced to a single embossed letterform, sometimes expanded into an environmental graphic that fills an entire wall.

title: FNF 40 Years in Jordan
seoTitle: FNF 40 Years in Jordan — Branding & Design | Lōn Visuals
lede: Forty years of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom in Jordan, marked by an anniversary identity that honours the foundation's legacy, sits seamlessly within its modern brand, and sets a bold tone for what comes next.
info: Logo, Identity system, Print, Digital, Event

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.title: Four decades of liberal values
paras: Since 1984, the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom has advanced liberal values in Jordan, promoting democracy, human rights, civic education and a free-market economy. Working with ministries, civil society organisations and partners across the country, it has built initiatives that drive change and empower communities.

The 40th anniversary called for an identity that honours that legacy while sitting seamlessly within FNF's modern brand: one that captures the spirit of partnership and progress, and carries the foundation's vision for a freer, more prosperous Jordan into its next chapter.

blocks.label: The Idea
blocks.title: Drawn from the F
paras: The 40 is built on the grid of FNF's own symbol. The slanted F is extended into the two numerals, keeping its angle, its rounded corners and its forward lean, so the anniversary mark reads as part of the foundation rather than an addition to it.
Blue carries the history; magenta marks the celebration. A bilingual line completes the lockup: Years of Collaboration, FNF – Jordan, أربعين عاماً من التعاون.
From concept to execution, the work spans the logo, a complete visual identity system and branding elements built to travel across digital and physical platforms.

title: Sky Falcons
lede: SkyFalcons is a premium aviation brokerage that connects clients worldwide with world-class aviation support services — covering aircraft sales, leasing, financing, maintenance, consulting, and private charter.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.title: Where luxury meets altitude
paras: The brand needed to communicate the rare intersection of luxury and precision that defines private aviation. The identity had to feel exclusive without being inaccessible — refined and modern, yet bold enough to signal authority in a high-stakes industry.

The solution centers on a custom falcon symbol — drawn from the natural geometry of a falcon in full dive — angular, sharp, and unmistakably in motion. Paired with a clean serif wordmark and anchored in Sand Gold (#B4A060) against deep black, the identity reads as premium, mature, and globally confident.

title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates
lede: One visual language for Jordan's voice abroad: the branding and visual identity guidelines that bring the Ministry, its 59 diplomatic missions and its reach into 87 more countries under a single, consistent standard.
meta: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates
info: Identity system, Guidelines, Print, Digital, Events

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.title: The voice of a kingdom, abroad
paras: Established in 1939, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan represents the country through 59 diplomatic missions worldwide, with non-resident representation in a further 87 countries.

In 2013 it became the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates. The new name signalled a new duty: closer care for Jordanians living abroad, stronger channels of communication with them, and deeper ties to home. A dedicated department followed, and with it the need for an identity that could speak for both.

blocks.label: The Brief
blocks.title: Consistency is credibility
paras: For a ministry, visual presentation is never just design. It is a statement of what the state stands for, and every inconsistency across an embassy, a department or a feed reads as a crack in that statement.

The Branding and Visual Identity Guidelines give a decentralised institution one language: clear standards for the logo, colour, typography, photography and video that any unit, in any country, can apply with confidence, and that are never to be diluted, substituted or redrawn.

blocks.label: The Mark
blocks.title: One crest, two scripts
paras: The identity is anchored by the emblem of the Royal Hashemite Court, set above the Ministry's name in Thuluth, the classical script of the Kingdom's state institutions, and in Trajan, whose Roman capitals give the English line the same ceremonial weight.
Primary, landscape, Arabic-only and English-only versions cover every composition, each with defined clear space and approved use on white, dark and maroon grounds.

title: Sana Interiors
lede: A complete identity reconstruction for a growing interior design studio — from a minimal Arabic wordmark to a refined, contemporary monogram with architectural depth.

blocks.label: Project Overview
blocks.title: From a personal signature to a complete visual identity built for scale.
paras: Sana Interiors began with a simple Arabic logo that served the early stage of the brand. As the studio grew into a recognised name in residential and commercial interior design, the need for a stronger, more premium presence became clear.

The new identity was developed from the ground up — introducing a distinctive SI monogram, a refined custom logotype, and a full visual system grounded in the textures and materials of architectural space.

blocks.label: The Icon
blocks.title: S meets I — a fluid architectural fusion.
paras: The visual icon was developed by abstractly merging the initials S and I. Rather than a literal typographic mark, the letters were transformed into a fluid architectural form where curves and vertical structure interact to create a balanced symbol.

The vertical element represents structure and stability, while the flowing S-curve introduces movement and spatial harmony — reflecting the relationship between architecture and the interior space it contains.
